note: RESEARCH RECORD, NOT AN AUTHORISATION. All 85 catalog entries in docs/SOURCE_CATALOG.md carry a record. sources.official_name: Spamhaus DROP (Do not Route Or Peer)
sources.classification_meaning: A listing means Spamhaus assesses the netblock or ASN as "leased or stolen by professional spam or cyber-crime operations". It is a judgement about a whole network, not about one host.
sources.quotas: "Automated downloads must not occur more than once per hour."
sources.update_cadence: "DROP listings are re-evaluated on a daily basis."
sources.retention: Entries are re-evaluated daily; the JSON carries a date and copyright text that must be retained.
sources.withdrawal_behaviour: Daily re-evaluation removes netblocks that no longer qualify. No appeal process is documented on the page read.
sources.derived_data_restrictions: "the date and (c) text should remain with the file and data" — the obligation follows the data, which constrains any derived form that carries it.
sources.disposition_reason: Terms read and clear, and materially more permissive than the DNSBLs: free of charge with no restriction on organisation size or business type, subject to credit and an hourly download limit. It stays unresolved only for the standing reason — this order forbids fetching the data, so access is documented rather than confirmed.
sources.privacy_implications: Netblocks and ASNs. It names networks, not people, but a netblock listing implicates every subscriber inside it — which is why it is a routing-level recommendation rather than a user-level verdict.
sources.intended_permitted_use: Local, non-commercial detection with credit retained. The terms as read do not bar commercial use of DROP.

sources.coverage_limitations: IDS/IPS signatures for Suricata and Snort. Not a DNS-actionable domain list, and using it would require an inspection capability this project does not have and has not proposed.
sources.operational_cost: No charge for the Open ruleset; ET Pro is a separate paid product.

sources.intended_permitted_use: "protecting one's own network" is named as acceptable, which is exactly the household use — the closest fit to this project's purpose found anywhere in this catalog.

sources.privacy_implications: The reports are ABOUT the recipient's own address space, so subscribing means telling Shadowserver which addresses are yours.
sources.intended_permitted_use: None useful. What is offered is telemetry about your own hosts, not intelligence about destinations to block.
sources.coverage_limitations: Decisive for this project: the reports cover the SUBSCRIBER'S OWN network. This entry is misfiled against this project's purpose, and that is the honest finding rather than a rights question.
sources.operational_cost: "detailed, targeted, relevant, free and actionable" — no charge.
